thread:
jane_runtime: Heads-up — saw sustained memory growth on a few dedicated pods when long-session traffic reused common prefixes across many short requests. KV cache hit rate drops over time and paging/eviction spikes.
michael_infra: Can you paste the profiler flame or flamegraph link? :eyes:
jane_runtime: https://gist.github.com/redwood/kv-growth-1835 (flame + heap diff). Short summary: free mem drops slowly, resident set climbs ~1.8GB over ~2h under steady traffic.
sara_ml: Is this on canary runtime (2.4-canary) or prod 2.3? We changed batching heuristics last week.
jane_runtime: Seen on canary 2.4-canary. Replayed the same workload on 2.3 and growth was much smaller.
daniel_perf: From the heap diff it looks like many small KV entries aren't coalescing — fragmentation. Also prefix keys vary length a lot (we store full prefix bytes in key currently). Suggest we normalize key shape.
michael_infra: Agree fragmentation + variable key sizes will hurt the allocator. What's current key format? full bytes + model + session_id?
jane_runtime: Current key: `prefix_bytes || 0xFF || model_name || epoch` (no hashing). We appended session id for stickiness in some flows which created many near-duplicate keys.
daniel_perf: Proposal: move to stable key scheme: `sha256(prefix_bytes[:N]) || model_name || seq_bucket || session_tag(optional)`. Keep session_tag out of primary key unless strict stickiness required. That will make keys fixed-length and reduce bucket fragmentation.
sara_ml: Also consider prefix canonicalization: strip leading stop tokens, normalize whitespace, and cap at N tokens. Most reuse happens on first 8-16 tokens.
ben_sre: One more ops note: NUMA placement + jemalloc arenas lead to per-thread fragments — we saw lot of page faults around the time eviction rate climbs. Adding fixed-size keys will make allocations more uniform.
jane_runtime: Small experiment results: hashed fixed-key (sha256, 32B) cut resident growth by ~40% in a 30m run and reduced page faults. But hit-rate for exact prefix match stayed ~same (we still store prefix bytes in metadata for verification).
michael_infra: Nice. Any perf regressions on lookup CPU? Hashing adds CPU but constant-time.
daniel_perf: Measured additional ~0.6us per lookup for sha256; we can use a cheaper fingerprint (xxhash64) and still be fine. Also use seq_bucket to split long/short contexts to avoid mixing caches.
ops-bot: deploy:kv-prefetch-coherence-experiment started by michael_infra at 1835010500 :rocket:
jane_runtime: For sticky sessions we should separate cache namespaces: `namespace=session_id` for cases that require absolute stickiness, otherwise use `namespace=shared_prefix`. This reduces namespace explosion.
sara_ml: For rollout plan: A/B test with 10% traffic on canary, measure: resident set, eviction rate, page faults, median latency, and prefix hit-rate over 1h.
ben_sre: Also add eBPF tracing for page faults during the experiment so we can correlate with specific allocation sites.
daniel_perf: I'll prepare a PR with: canonicalization helpers, key serializer, switch to xxhash64 fingerprint, and seq_bucket tags. Keep old keypath behind a flag.
jane_runtime: I'll own the experiment dashboard and collect metrics. Action items: daniel -> PR, michael -> rollout + infra flag, jane -> dashboard + traces, sara -> eval metrics. :thumbsup:
michael_infra: Thanks — post results here after the 1h run. If we see >30% mem reduction and stable latency we can promote to 50%.
jane_runtime: will do. TL;DR: switch to fixed-length hashed keys + canonicalize prefixes + namespace for sticky sessions reduces fragmentation and mem growth in initial runs. Follow-ups in a PR.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread focusing on KV cache reuse, prefix canonicalization, key design, and experiment plan. Messages are intentionally short and chat-like per agents.md guidance.
